predecessors.name: Second Turkic Khaganate
predecessors.text: the Second Turkic Khaganate's Mongolian heartland: the Basmyls took Ötüken in 744 and 'Later that year a Uyghur-Karluk alliance defeats them'; in 745 the Uyghurs killed Kulun Beg, 'the last Göktürk…

successors.name: Yenisei Kyrgyz
successors.text: the Kyrgyz shape of 840, the Orkhon valley and Tuva, after the Kyrgyz 'sacked Ordu-Baliq' in 840

successors.name: Ganzhou Uyghur Kingdom
successors.text: 'the Uyghurs migrated south and established the Ganzhou Uyghur Kingdom in modern Gansu'

successors.name: Kingdom of Qocho
successors.text: the Turfan basin around Gaochang, where the refugees founded the Kingdom of Qocho

successors.name: Kara-Khanid Khanate
successors.text: no land passed: the page lists the Kara-Khanid Khanate as successor and says 'a third group went to seek refuge among the Karluks'

ledger.x: 744: the Uyghurs and Karluks defeat the Basmyls at Ötüken and found the Uyghur Khaganate.
745: the last Göktürk khagan is killed.
746: the Karluk yabghu submits to the Uyghurs.
751: the Tang withdraw after Talas and Turfan passes to the Uyghurs.
766: the Karluks emerge as an independent khanate under a Yabghu in Zhetysu.
766: the Karluks end the Türgesh in Zhetysu.
789: the Karluks annex the Futu Valley.
790: Tibet defeats the Uyghurs and Tang at Tingzhou.
808: last dated Uyghur gain from Tibet.
840: the Kyrgyz throw off the Uyghurs.

wars.name: Uyghur revolt against the Second Turkic Khaganate
wars.outcome: The Uyghurs, Karluks and Basmyls rebelled in 742; the Basmyls took Ötüken and killed Özmiş Khagan in 744, then a Uyghur-Karluk alliance defeated them and founded the khaganate; Kulun Beg, the last Göktürk khagan, was killed in 745.

wars.name: Uyghur subjugation of the Kyrgyz
wars.outcome: Bayanchur destroyed Kyrgyz trading outposts, defeated their army and executed their khan; the Kyrgyz became Uyghur vassals until 840.

wars.name: Uyghur intervention in the An Lushan Rebellion
wars.outcome: About 4,000 Uyghur horsemen helped retake Chang'an and Luoyang in 757 (Luoyang looted for three days); Bögü aided the Tang again at Luoyang in 762.

wars.name: Uyghur-Tibetan wars over the Tarim and Dzungaria
wars.outcome: Tibet beat the Uyghurs and Tang at Tingzhou (790); the Uyghurs beat Tibetans and Karluks at Beiting (791), took Gaochang (792, 803) and seized Liang Province (808); Tibetan attacks of 816, 821, 823 and 832 changed no ground on the page.

wars.name: Kyrgyz conquest of the Uyghur Khaganate
wars.outcome: Kulug Bagha, a rival of the usurper Qasar, invited the Kyrgyz; about 80,000 horsemen sacked Ordu-Baliq in 840, Qasar was executed and the khaganate collapsed.

wars.name: Tang-Uyghur war of the refugees
wars.outcome: Wujie invaded Shaanxi in 841; Shi Xiong's Tang army killed 10,000 at Shahu on 13 February 843; Wujie was killed in 846 and Enian decisively defeated in 847.

certainty.note: A steppe empire: the Shiwei, Altai and Gobi limits are the New Book of Tang's description, not a surveyed line; the western and Tarim frontiers moved with the Tibetan wars (790-808) and are the softest.
